module_title: Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009: Constitutional Basis & Core Mandates
introduction: This foundational level establishes the constitutional journey of the Right to Education. It details the precise definitions of 'Free' and 'Compulsory' education, the specific age groups targeted, and the absolute prohibitions placed on schools and teachers.

core_concepts.title: Constitutional Background
core_concepts.description:
Education was originally in the State List but was moved to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002)** was the historic milestone that made education a Fundamental Right. 
- It inserted **Article 21A**, which states: 'The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.'
- The RTE Act 2009 is the enabling legislation that operationalized Article 21A. It came into force on **April 1, 2010** (except in the state of Jammu & Kashmir).

core_concepts.title: Decoding 'Free' and 'Compulsory'
core_concepts.description:
1. Free Education: No child shall be liable to pay any kind of fee, charge, or expense that may prevent them from pursuing and completing elementary education (Class 1 to 8). Textbooks, uniforms, and mid-day meals are covered.
2. Compulsory Education: It is the legal obligation of the appropriate government and local authorities to ensure the admission, attendance, and completion of elementary education for all children in the 6-14 age group.

core_concepts.title: Strict Prohibitions (Bans) under RTE
core_concepts.description:
The Act strictly prohibits several historical practices to protect children:
1. Physical punishment and mental harassment (Section 17).
2. Screening procedures for admission of children or parents (No interviews or tests) (Section 13).
3. Capitation fees (Donations for admission) (Section 13).
4. Private tuition by school teachers (Section 28).
5. Running a school without recognition (Section 18).

core_concepts.title: Age-Appropriate Admission
core_concepts.description: If a child above 6 years of age has never been admitted to any school, or dropped out before completing elementary education, the RTE Act mandates that they must be admitted to a class **appropriate to their age** (Section 4), NOT to Class 1. They have a right to receive special training to catch up with their peers.

important_entities.name: Target Age Group vs. CWSN Target Age Group
important_entities.key_fact: RTE targets 6-14 years normally, but 6-18 years for Children with Special Needs (CWSN).
important_entities.significance: A heavily tested distinction. While a regular child gets free education from age 6 to 14, the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act integrates with RTE to extend this fundamental right for disabled children up to the age of **18 years**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will often ask 'When was the RTE Act passed?' vs 'When did the RTE Act come into force?'. It was passed by the Parliament in August 2009, but it officially came into effect on **April 1, 2010**. Always read the verb (passed vs. implemented) carefully.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 13 bans Money & Tests, 17 bans Beating, 28 bans Tuitions
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
In advanced exams (like DSSSB), exact sections are asked. 
- Sec 13: Capitation & Screening
- Sec 17: Corporal Punishment
- Sec 28: Private Tuitions

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a pedagogy question presents a scenario where a 10-year-old child who has never studied applies for admission, ALWAYS select the option that places the child in **Class 5** (Age-appropriate admission: 10 years - 5 = Class 5), along with 'Special Training'.
